hints: Set up the definite integral for the area under the curve between $x = 0$ and $x = 4$: $\int_0^4 (10x^{1/2} - \frac{5}{2}x^{3/2})\, dx$.
Integrate each term using the power rule: $\int 10x^{1/2} dx = \frac{20}{3}x^{3/2}$ and $\int \frac{5}{2}x^{3/2} dx = x^{5/2}$.
Evaluate the antiderivative between limits $x = 0$ and $x = 4$.
walkthrough:
Set up the definite integral for the area bounded by the curve and the $x$-axis between $x = 0$ and $x = 4$:
$$\text{Area} = \int_0^4 \left(10x^{1/2} - \frac{5}{2}x^{3/2}\right) dx$$

Integrate term by term using the power rule:
$$\int 10x^{1/2}\, dx = 10 \cdot \frac{x^{3/2}}{3/2} = \frac{20}{3}x^{3/2}$$
$$\int \frac{5}{2}x^{3/2}\, dx = \frac{5}{2} \cdot \frac{x^{5/2}}{5/2} = x^{5/2}$$
$$\text{Antiderivative} = \left[ \frac{20}{3}x^{3/2} - x^{5/2} \right]_0^4$$

Subtract the value at the lower limit $x = 0$:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{64}{3} - 0 = \frac{64}{3} = 21\frac{1}{3}$$

ai_rubric.Finding Areas Under Curves: Integrates $10x^{1/2} - \frac{5}{2}x^{3/2}$ to $\frac{20}{3}x^{3/2} - x^{5/2}$ and evaluates limits $0$ to $4$ to obtain $\frac{64}{3}$ (or $21\frac{1}{3}$).
